actions.body: Research trajectories are often hindered by the 'sunk cost effect,' described as occurring "on an important human decision bias – the sunk cost effect. To address our research question, we use a unique a" (source-3cd9e0756c2c4cca). This bias obscures the rational evaluation of epistemic progress. Planning models further demonstrate this complication: "or abandon it. We model planning tasks in which an agent with this type of bias tries to reach a designated goa" (source-4fb70d1c1dd147da). To mitigate these biases, adaptive frameworks—modeled after sustainable heritage conservation (source-c5e9e9da1ebf41eb)—provide a structure for periodic re-evaluation rather than blind commitment. Abandonment is therefore not a failure of persistence but a calculated reallocation of resources.
actions.lede: Intelligence requires systematic methods to distinguish between persistence in a difficult pursuit and the sunk cost effect that leads to diminishing returns.
